text:
To solve the questions, let's first determine the dimensions and properties given in the drawing and prompt:
- **Dimensions (outside face of wall):** Length = 48'-0", Width = 26'-0"
- **Perimeter ($P$):** $2 \times (48\text{ ft} + 26\text{ ft}) = 148\text{ ft}$
- **Wall Height ($H$):** $8\text{ ft}$
- **CMU Nominal Size:** 8 in high $\times$ 16 in long (face area of one CMU = $8/12 \times 16/12 = 0.8889\text{ ft}^2$, or $1.125\text{ blocks/ft}^2$).
- **Wall Surface Area:** $148\text{ ft} \times 8\text{ ft} = 1184\text{ ft}^2$

---

### **Q1. Number of CMUs including 6% waste**
- Number of blocks per square foot for standard stretcher = $1.125\text{ blocks/ft}^2$ (or more precisely, $1 / (1.333\text{ ft} \times 0.667\text{ ft}) = 1.125$).
- Total theoretical blocks = $1184\text{ ft}^2 \times 1.125\text{ blocks/ft}^2 = 1332\text{ blocks}$.
- Including 6% waste: $1332 \times 1.06 = 1411.92 \approx 1412\text{ CMUs}$.

---

### **Q2. Fully grouted grout volume including 10% waste**
- Rate = $0.17\text{ ft}^3$ per CMU.
- Total number of CMUs (theoretical) = $1332\text{ blocks}$.
- Total theoretical grout volume = $1332 \times 0.17\text{ ft}^3 = 226.44\text{ ft}^3$.
- Including 10% waste: $226.44 \times 1.10 = 249.084\text{ ft}^3$.
- Convert to cubic yards ($27\text{ ft}^3 = 1\text{ CY}$): 
  $249.084 / 27 = 9.225\text{ CY} \approx 9.23\text{ CY}$.

---

### **Q3. Grout volume with vertical reinforcement at 24 in o.c. including 10% waste**
- Vertical cells at 24 in (2 ft) on center.
- Perimeter = 148 ft. Number of vertical cells = $148\text{ ft} / 2\text{ ft} = 74\text{ cells}$.
- Wall height = 8 ft. Since standard blocks are 8 inches tall ($0.667\text{ ft}$), there are $8 / 0.667 = 12$ courses.
- Each vertical cell runs the full height of the wall (8 ft).
- Fully grouted volume for the whole wall (all cells) uses 1332 blocks $\times 0.17\text{ ft}^3 = 226.44\text{ ft}^3$. 
- A standard 16" CMU has 2 cores. Therefore, total cores in the wall = $1332\text{ blocks} \times 2\text{ cores/block} = 2664\text{ cores}$.
- Volume per core = $226.44\text{ ft}^3 / 2664\text{ cores} = 0.085\text{ ft}^3/\text{core}$ (or since each block has 2 cores, 1 block volume of grout = $0.17\text{ ft}^3$, so 1 core = $0.085\text{ ft}^3$).
- Number of grouted cores (cells) = 74 continuous vertical stacks of cores from bottom to top. Each stack has 12 courses, meaning 12 core spaces per vertical interval.
- Total grouted cores = 74 vertical locations $\times$ 12 courses = 888 cores.
- Theoretical grout volume = $888\text{ cores} \times 0.085\text{ ft}^3/\text{core} = 75.48\text{ ft}^3$.
- Including 10% waste: $75.48 \times 1.10 = 83.028\text{ ft}^3$.
- Convert to cubic yards: 
  $83.028 / 27 = 3.075\text{ CY} \approx 3.08\text{ CY}$.

---

FINAL: Q1 = 1412 CMU
FINAL: Q2 = 9.23 CY
FINAL: Q3 = 3.08 CY
